notes.note: This Decalogue text contains double accent, the text is also in poor condition. The mark in question is a broken line coming out of the rightmost leg of the sin. notes.note: At question is the reddish upper dot of an apparent zaqef-qatan over the yod/vav. Two approaches are available, the first assumes the dot was once deliberately placed by the scribe. The first approach says that the reddish dot is probably the upper dot of a zaqaf-qatan over the yod displaced because of interference from a merkha from a word, סַלֵּ֥י, on the previous line. The second approach says the reddish dot is an anomaly unintended by the scribe, leaving a single dot over both the yod and the vav. A single dot over the yod would need to be a revia and second dot on the vav would be a holam. This transcription prefers the first approach because of a lack of other reddish dots in the sheet containing the text and the fact the dot is well-placed and well-sized. Also, the second approach's dot over the yod has no outstanding revia characteristics, such as a diamond shape. A note 't' is added, however.
